ctbids-50250-5881554.description:
A 7-inch 45 RPM single by Kenny Rogers and the First Edition on the orange Reprise Records “Back to Back Hits” label with the riverboat logo. One side is the classic “Ruby, Don’t Take Your Love to Town,” written by Mel Tillis, produced by Jimmy Bowen, and arranged by Glen D. Hardin. The other side is the story-song favorite “Reuben James,” written by Harvey and Etris and arranged and produced by Mike Post. It comes in an olive gold Philadelphia International Records “The Sound of Philadelphia” company sleeve with the bold magenta logo. It would make a great addition to a country or country-pop 45 collection, a jukebox, or a retro music display.
Details:
Style: 7-inch 45 RPM Back to Back Hits single in a company paper sleeve
Color: Black vinyl with an orange Reprise label and riverboat logo, plus an olive gold sleeve with magenta and brown print
Size: About 7 in across (see tape measure photo)
Marks: Reprise Back to Back Hits 0738; L6669 (Ruby, Don’t Take Your Love to Town, 2:52, Spring ‘69) and M17354 (Reuben James, 2:44, Fall ‘69); Made in U.S.A.
Condition:
The record is flat and keeps a glossy finish. The vinyl has light surface scuffs and faint handling marks that show under light, plus a small mark near the label on the “Reuben James” side. Both labels are bright, with sharp, readable print and no writing or stickers. There are a few small dark specks near the center hole on the “Ruby” side. The Philadelphia International sleeve is not the original Reprise sleeve. It has light toning, soft creasing, a small white mark near one top corner, and light wear along the edges and corners. It still holds and protects the record well. Please review all photos. Sold as shown.
